sections.html:
Clinton is a Hinds County city in the Jackson metro area, home to 28,100 residents at the 2020 count. Interstate 20, U.S. Route 80 and the Natchez Trace Parkway cross it, with I-20 exits at Springridge Road, Clinton-Raymond Road and the Parkway. The Clinton Public School District serves the city.

Homes here sell in a tight market: the homeowner vacancy rate was 1.4 percent, while rentals ran looser at 8.4 percent vacant. Many sellers are landlords, heirs of an older house or owners with a house that needs work before a lender will approve it.

Tornadoes are the weather event buyers think about in central Mississippi. An EF3 tornado struck Clinton on April 15, 2011, damaged the area near Interstate 20 and injured ten people. One storm does not predict the next, but it explains why buyers and insurers ask about roof condition, windows and tree trimming.

  • Write down the roof's age and any past claims, and keep the paperwork.
  • Photograph repairs before and after.
  • Trim limbs that overhang the roof and remove dead trees.
  • Ask your insurer for a loss history if a buyer requests one.

The city requires permits and inspections for construction through Community Development, so check with that office before you do storm repairs beyond simple patching.

sections.h2: Rental registration for landlords who sell
sections.html:
Clinton requires every rental property to be registered, and a rental license is not valid until the unit passes inspection. The rule covers manufactured homes, single-family houses, multifamily units and any residential property leased to someone other than the owner.

  • Anyone renting one or more units must hold a rental license.
  • Registration is annual for each unit.
  • Owners agree to inspection by a city inspector, with prior notice so the tenant can be told.
  • A Certificate of Occupancy is withheld until the problems are repaired and the unit is re-inspected.

Inspectors look at junk cars, dead vegetation, debris, landscaping, building maintenance, graffiti, refuse facilities, unpermitted construction, dilapidated structures and substandard conditions. A landlord who is selling should clear those items and keep the registration current. A buyer who plans to keep the tenant takes over the compliance duty.

Clinton set up an Environmental Court to move code cases along faster than the regular municipal court could. It hears derelict properties, tree ordinance violations, vandalism, building and fire code violations and other maintenance problems on private, commercial and residential property. The mayor has said such cases once took about six months and could become a cycle of citation after citation.

An unkept vacant house is the kind of property that ends up there. Complaints come in through the city's request form, and Community Development inspects. If you own a vacant inherited house, an open case complicates a listing and a financed sale. After an inspection, the city sends a report listing the problems and a date for compliance, so respond in writing before that date.

Real property taxes in Hinds County are due on or before February 1 for property assessed the year before. The Tax Assessor lists values, the Tax Collector bills and collects, and the Chancery Clerk sends the assessor every recorded deed so ownership on the roll stays current.

Ownership is set as of January 1. The assessor presents the roll to the Board of Supervisors by the first Monday in July, and the usual appeal deadline is the first Monday in August.

  • The assessor reviews 25 percent of taxable property each year, so every parcel gets a look at least once every four years.
  • For most homes the review is a drive-by, and the appraiser contacts the owner only when what is seen differs from the file.
  • Appraisal notices have historically gone out when a value rises by $2,000 or more, and for new assessments.
  • Interior inspections of residences are not required.

Hinds County has two judicial districts, each with its own tax collector and assessor office. The First Judicial District office is in Jackson at 316 S. President Street, and the Second Judicial District office is in Raymond at 127 W. Main Street. Ask which one handles your parcel before you call. The Hinds County Tax Assessor page describes the appeal process. If February 1 falls on a weekend or legal holiday, paying the next Monday avoids penalties and interest.

sections.h2: The deed and who may draft it
sections.html:
The Chancery Clerk records the deed, and Mississippi limits who can write one. Preparing a deed of conveyance for a fee is the practice of law under Miss. Code Ann. 73-3-55, so use a Mississippi attorney, usually through a closing attorney or title company.

Recording standards are specific. The instrument needs the preparer's name, address and telephone number, and an attorney-prepared instrument must carry the attorney's Mississippi Bar number. Hinds County collects the $1.00 archive fee, so a deed usually costs $26.00, including indexing for the first five pages.

The state disclosure statute applies too. Under Section 89-1-503, a seller who delivers the property condition statement after an offer lets the buyer withdraw within three days of personal delivery or five days of mailing.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a fit for a Clinton house?
sections.html:
It can be, when the house has code problems, a tenant or a repair list that would delay a conventional closing. Cash Home Buyers reviews Clinton houses in their current condition, including homes with open code notices, so you do not have to finish repairs before an offer.

A cash sale keeps every legal step. Expect a contract, a title search, a deed prepared by a Mississippi attorney or title company, and recording in the Hinds County land records. Before you choose, compare an as-is offer with the cost and time of fixing the house and listing it. Ask for the offer in writing and for the date by which it expires.

faqs.q: Does Clinton require rental properties to be registered?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Rental Property Ordinance requires annual registration for each unit and an inspection before a rental license is valid. It covers single-family houses, multifamily units and manufactured homes.

faqs.q: What happens if my Clinton house has a code violation?
faqs.a: The city sends an inspection report listing the problems and a compliance date. Persistent cases can go to Clinton's Environmental Court.

faqs.q: When are Hinds County property taxes due?
faqs.a: On or before February 1 for property assessed the year before. If that date falls on a weekend or legal holiday, paying the next Monday avoids penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Who can draft a deed in Mississippi?
faqs.a: A Mississippi attorney, typically through a closing attorney or title company. Under Miss. Code Ann. 73-3-55, drafting a deed of conveyance for a fee is the practice of law.

faqs.q: Which Hinds County office serves Clinton property?
faqs.a: Hinds County has First and Second Judicial District offices, in Jackson and Raymond. Ask the Tax Assessor or Tax Collector which one covers your parcel before you call.
